title: Put a knife away handle-first so the next person grabs the handle
instruction: Put the knife away in the empty slot of the knife tray in the drawer.
context: In kitchens and labs a knife is put away with its handle toward the person who reaches in next and the blade away from them, so nobody's hand closes on an edge. The instruction doesn't say which way round; the two knives already in the tray lie handle-front, and the loose knife starts with its blade toward the robot, so stowing it safely means turning it half a turn, which one gripper can't do in one go.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Cutting board (light wood, 30 x 30 x 1.5 cm, fixed) from x = 0.12 to 0.42 and y = -0.17 to 0.13. Kitchen knife (90 g, 22 cm long): a dark-brown wooden handle 10 cm long, 2.4 cm wide and 2.2 cm thick, and a steel blade 12 cm long, 2.8 cm wide (tapering to 1.6 cm over its last 2 cm, the spine in line with one side of the handle), modelled 4 mm thick. It lies flat on its side on the board, along x, blade toward the robot: the bolster (where blade meets handle) at (0.265, -0.03), the tip at x = 0.145, the butt end of the handle at x = 0.365. Drawer (light birch, open top, fixed, standing on the table), outside x = 0.16 to 0.482 and y = 0.158 to 0.466: a 1 cm floor, walls 5 cm tall, the front panel (2 cm thick, facing the robot, with an 8 x 1.2 cm dark pull 1.5 cm proud of it at y = 0.312) and three 1.2 cm walls; inside x = 0.18 to 0.47. The knife tray in it has three slots along x, 8.8 cm wide inside, separated by two darker wooden dividers 1 cm wide and 1.5 cm tall: slot 1 (empty, nearest the board) y = 0.170 to 0.258, slot 2 y = 0.268 to 0.356, slot 3 y = 0.366 to 0.454. Slot 2 holds a paring knife (black handle 10 x 2.4 x 2.2 cm, blade 11 x 2.5 cm) and slot 3 a chef's knife (black handle 12 x 2.6 x 2.2 cm, blade 14 x 4 cm), both lying flat with the handle's butt end 2.5 cm from the front panel, handle toward the front. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start in the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: 0 if the knife goes off the table at any time (any part of it 5 cm or more below the table top). Otherwise, at the end, with the robot let go of the knife (no gripper closed to under 3 cm within 3 cm of its centre line): 1.0 if it lies in slot 1 (every part between the slot's dividers and inside the drawer, its lowest point within 5 mm of the tray floor), flat (its length within 10 degrees of horizontal), with the handle toward the drawer front (handle to tip, seen from above, within 20 degrees of straight back); 0.5 if it lies anywhere in the drawer (every part inside the walls, its lowest point below their top) but not all of that, e.g. blade toward the front, in the wrong slot, across a divider or propped up; 0.25 if it was lifted at some point (its lowest point 3 cm or more above the board) but doesn't end let go in the drawer; else 0. The trial ends with 1.0 once the 1.0 condition holds with the knife still for 2 s. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lay the knife back on the board in its start position (blade toward the robot) and check the stored knives are handle-front in slots 2 and 3. For real-world trials use a blunted or training knife.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The knife is one compound rigid body of three boxes (handle and a two-part blade); its blade is 4 mm thick (a real one is 1.5-2 mm) for stable contact, and its underside is one flat face (handle and blade flush), so it lies flat without rocking; a real knife lies on its handle's side and the blade's flat at a few degrees. Its mass is spread evenly over the shapes, so it balances 3 cm behind the bolster (a real one nearer the bolster). Rubber-like grip friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The board, drawer, tray and the two stored knives are fixed boxes; on a real table the board and drawer should be clamped or non-slip. Let-go and placement are judged by geometry from the robot's measured joints and the knife's pose, as from a video. Sim behaviour not yet measured in Isaac Sim.
